Variants.Content: King's Harbor is located on Pyke Island and is an important port and market in the Iron Islands. The "king" in the name indicates that this place is closely related to the power of the island's lords, but the port is not just a hall: shipwrights, oarsmen, fishermen, salt merchants, shepherds and warriors returning from voyages all met here. The harbor allowed the longships to replenish, repair, and regroup, and also allowed foreign cloth, food, iron, and rumors to enter the barren archipelago. For the Ironborn, the sea is not only ancestors, road and tomb; King's Harbor is therefore a political symbol and the most practical place of livelihood.
Entry Lordsport Local families also relied on salt fish, ore, barren fields, sheltered anchorages, and longships to return home; if any road, well, or dock failed, the price would fall first on them.

Entry Lordsport They will also recognize the accents, laws and credentials of the Iron Islands; reputations may travel great distances from taverns, but true distances must still be measured by wheel, oar or horse's hoof.

Entry Lordsport If you can supply supplies, avoid danger, and find a guide, it is worth marking in your itinerary; if you don't have these three things, no matter how loud your family name is, it won't be able to save the lost.
Entry Lordsport A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry Lordsport They care about salt fish, ore, barren fields, sheltered anchorages, and the return of longships. They also look at whether seeds are left after collecting grain and whether the city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see coats of arms, what they see is whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
